Run from the checkout with a configured build folder: python3 tools/mutate.py tests/data/submissions_mutants.json --keep-going --jobs 1 --timeout 600. Every mutant must be caught: each breaks one rule of docs/MAP_SUBMISSIONS.md (the server's own check, the canonical file, a limit, a protected name, the token, the session cookie's time, CSRF, what a visitor is told, a text rule, the door's size and method rules). The test command runs the three suites of the store, the routes and the text rules, and the door cases of test_ctl. Not listed on purpose: a longer-than-45-characters address text (inet_pton refuses any such text anyway, so the cap is a second lock and the mutant is equivalent). The two mutants fits_not_required and canonical_not_rechecked are second locks behind check_map's own 'works' and the canonical rewrite: a map that works but does not fit the place cannot be built from the map maker's output, and the rewritten file is checked again only as defense in depth; they are expected to survive. short_secret_accepted is not listed either: the owner's API is off in two places (the constructor and owner_api_on(), both at 32 characters), so changing one of them changes nothing a caller can see; the tests of a 31-character secret hold the pair. The mutants of the accounts, the roles, the sign-in and the CSRF token are tests/data/admin_accounts_mutants.json.
